title: Are You a Courageous Person?
summaryZh: 勇敢不是沒有恐懼，而是帶著神同在的應許，即使害怕也繼續前進。
lines: I used to always wonder if people considered me a courageous person.
我以前總是想知道，別人是否認為我是個勇敢的人。
Most people probably wouldn't think themselves courageous.
大多數人可能不會認為自己是勇敢的。
We tend to reserve that title for others.
我們往往把這個頭銜保留給別人。
At least, I know I did.
至少，我知道我以前是這樣。
But I could certainly point to more times in my life when I felt afraid than when I felt courageous.
但我確實可以指出，在我生命中感到害怕的時刻，比感到勇敢的時刻還要多。
I can think of moments in middle school where I was afraid to stand up for myself.
我能想起在國中時，我害怕為自己挺身而出的時刻。
Moments in college when I felt afraid to pursue full-time ministry because at the time my dad didn't approve.
還有在大學時，因為當時我父親不贊成，我害怕追求全職服事的時刻。
And even moments now in my adult life today where I'm afraid to mess up this whole parenting thing.
甚至現在在我成年的生活中，我也會害怕把教養孩子這件事搞砸。
I used to think having courage meant not being afraid, but I had it wrong.
我以前認為有勇氣意味著不害怕，但我弄錯了。
Having courage is not the absence of fear, but rather, having courage means moving forward even in the face of fear.
有勇氣並非沒有恐懼，相反地，有勇氣意味著即使面對恐懼也能繼續前進。
Courageous people do, in fact, feel fear, but they are compelled to push through their fear.
勇敢的人事實上也會感到恐懼，但他們被驅使著去克服恐懼。
That means you can't have courage without fear.
那意味著如果沒有恐懼，你就無法擁有勇氣。
勇敢的人是帶著恐懼去做的。
One of my favorite characters in all of Scripture is a guy named Gideon.
在整本聖經中，我最喜歡的人物之一是一個名叫基甸的人。
And I think I like him so much because of how relatable he is.
我想我這麼喜歡他，是因為他非常令人有共鳴。
We are introduced to Gideon in the book of Judges during a time when Israel finds itself under the oppression of the Midianites.
我們在士師記中認識了基甸，當時以色列正處於米甸人的壓迫之下。
The odds were stacked against Israel.
當時的局勢對以色列非常不利。
They were constantly living in fear.
他們一直生活在恐懼之中。
And God has chosen Gideon to lead Israel into battle against them.
神揀選了基甸帶領以色列人與他們爭戰。
He gives God all the valid reasons why he is not capable.
他給了神所有合理的原因，說明他為什麼沒有能力。
Honestly, you have to appreciate his self-awareness!
老實說，你不得不欣賞他的自我認知！
He knew what Gideon was and wasn't capable of.
祂知道基甸能做什麼，不能做什麼。
But God gave Gideon a promise that compelled Gideon to push through his fear and show courage.
但神給了基甸一個應許，驅使基甸克服恐懼，展現勇氣。
God promised Gideon, "I will be with you."
神應許基甸：「我必與你同在。」
And that truth rings true today.
這個真理在今天依然適用。
No matter what I face, no matter what I'm walking through, even when things aren't going the way my control-freak self had all planned out, or even when I'm down and hurting my God is still with me.
無論我面對什麼，無論我正在經歷什麼，即使事情沒有按照我這個控制狂原本計畫的那樣發展，甚至當我低落和痛苦時，我的神依然與我同在。
So I want to ask a question that could shake up your life in the best possible way: What would you do if you were confident that God was with you?
所以我想問一個問題，它可能會以最好的方式改變你的人生：如果你深信神與你同在，你會怎麼做？
For me the answer to that question has looked different during various seasons of my life.
對我來說，這個問題的答案在我人生的不同階段中看起來是不一樣的。
When I was in college it was standing up for my faith even when it cost me, and serving my church even when I felt unqualified.
當我在大學時，它是即使要付出代價也要為我的信仰挺身而出，並且即使覺得自己不夠資格也要服事我的教會。
More recently the answer to that question has looked like starting a college ministry and even navigating family drama and tension.
最近，這個問題的答案看起來像是開始一個大學生事工，甚至是處理家庭的紛爭與緊張關係。
What might it be for you?
對你來說那會是什麼呢？
What job would you accept or quit?
你會接受或辭去什麼工作？
What difficult conversation would you have?
你會去進行什麼困難的對話？
What relationship would you seek to reconcile?
你會尋求修復什麼樣的關係？
God is with you, for you, behind you.
神與你同在，支持你，在你身後。
And while His presence is not a guarantee of an outcome that we would deem successful, one thing is for sure: we'll not regret courageously taking a step of faith God is calling us towards.
雖然祂的同在並不能保證會有一個我們認為成功的結果，但有一件事是確定的：我們不會後悔勇敢地邁出神呼召我們踏出的信心步伐。
所以，讓我們帶著恐懼去做吧。
